en.title: Server Replacements After Three Consecutive Errors
en.description:
Observe each server's own requests separately; after three consecutive error results, replace the server and reset its consecutive error count to zero, and a success also resets it. Logs from other servers do not interrupt a server's consecutive requests.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m; each of the next m lines contains a server number (1-based) and success/error. 1≤n≤200, 1≤m≤20000; the upper bound on m follows a text transcription of a blurry image in the source and is not claimed to have been checked against the original image.
en.explanation: Example 1: s1 is replaced once when its third error occurs, followed by only one more error, so the answer is 1. Example 2: six errors in a row cause a replacement every three, so the answer is 2. Example 3: a success interrupts the consecutive errors, so the answer is 0.
hints: Store the consecutive error count for each server; success resets it to zero, and an error adds one, replacing the server and resetting the count when it reaches 3.
